title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses
why: Treats the agent harness (runtime software: context/memory, multi-turn control, tool sandboxes, verification) as the object of self-improvement: systems inspect their own traces, separate runtime bugs from model limits, and rewrite their own code. Proposes a unifying framework pairing four editable runtime components with a four-stage diagnose–patch–validate–deploy loop, argues against full-harness rewrites, and discusses defenses against prompt bloat, benchmark gaming, and evaluator tampering.
mechanism: Self-improving agent harnesses: a four-stage loop diagnoses failures, proposes code patches to four editable runtime components (context and state, agent control, action interfaces, verification and recovery), validates candidates, and deploys modular updates rather than rewriting the whole harness.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): experiments on SWE-bench Lite; gated modular evolution is reported to outperform prompt reflection and full-harness rewrites across models and repositories at a fraction of the token cost (full numeric tables not in the listing/abs excerpt).

title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
why: Execution-guided policy search that adapts the agent's execution harness (dispatch and physical plans) from cold-start measurements rather than a static plan. The QHI loop uses observed runtime responses to update dispatch, revise plans, and choose later experiments, and an independent confirmation panel controls policy replacement—retained harness policies under execution feedback.
mechanism: Self-evolving execution harness: a QHI loop updates runtime dispatch and physical plans from firsthand measurements, with an independent confirmation panel gating policy replacement.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): with fixed dispatch, a revised materialization policy reduces complete-delivery latency by 30.0% on one video-editing task across three fresh pairs. On held-out tasks, evolved policies reduce latency by 8.2% relative to the best fixed plan in one seed and by 4.6% relative to the initial proposal in another.

title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
why: JevRSI is a System-1/System-2 collaboration in which an asynchronous System-2 LLM develops a modular decision harness (procedures, state memory, and world models) while a low-latency System-1 model acts. Utility-driven retrieval selects modules by relevance and prior-task utility; environmental feedback guides targeted revisions so the harness recursively improves and System-2 interventions decrease as the harness evolves.
mechanism: Recursive improvement of a modular decision harness: System-2 develops procedures, state memory, and world models; utility-driven retrieval selects modules; environmental feedback triggers targeted revisions that are retained for later System-1 action.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): experiments across three datasets; JevRSI is reported to improve decision quality and match or surpass LLM agents in several settings while preserving low-latency execution. System-2 development interventions are reported to decrease as the harness evolves (full numeric tables not in the listing/abs excerpt).

title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators
why: Treats the reusable skill bank itself as the object of evolution rather than only accumulating skills from rollouts. Given hard-negative failures, EvoSkill-S1 applies five genetic-inspired operators (revision, cross-revision, mutation, dual-reflection, crossover) to parent skills; evaluator-guided write-back selectively retains beneficial child skills, with Skill Bank Fusion and a Procedural Skill Interface for transfer. The skill evolver is trained with downstream-task rewards, but the retained artifact is the skill bank.
mechanism: Direct evolution of a reusable skill bank: genetic-inspired operators produce child skills from hard-negative failures; evaluator-guided write-back retains beneficial updates; Skill Bank Fusion consolidates operator-specific banks and a Procedural Skill Interface supports transfer.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across reported math and code benchmarks, EvoSkill-S1 improves the corresponding initialized skill banks under both Qwen and GPT-family solvers, with relative gains of up to 12.39%. Compared with the strongest external baseline without direct skill evolution, the largest relative improvement reaches 20.39%.

title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
why: Formulates agent memory evolution as discovering which operator to apply, when, and how, instead of rewriting memory under a fixed operator schedule. A policy selects and instantiates four semantic operators (Abstract, Refine, Bridge, Reframe) from the current memory state and recent task history, updated with bi-level fitness (inner retrieval-quality vs complexity; outer strategic efficacy). The retained object is the evolved memory plus discovered operator strategy, evaluated online and in frozen transfer.
mechanism: Evolutionary strategy discovery for agent memory: a policy conditions on memory state and recent history to select and instantiate Abstract/Refine/Bridge/Reframe operators; bi-level fitness updates the policy while memory transformations are retained.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): under a one-pass online plus frozen-transfer protocol on ALFWorld, WebShop, and LifelongAgentBench (OS and DB), EvoDisco improves over memory baselines including MemP and MemRL. Largest reported gains are on ALFWorld (+8.8 online / +12.9 frozen-transfer points over MemP; +16.4 / +17.9 over MemRL). Ablations attribute gains to both fitness levels and the operator library.

title: When Agent Skills Go Stale: Runtime Behavior and Selective Maintenance in Evolving Environments
why: Studies what happens to retained agent skill state when the environment changes, and proposes selective maintenance: replay checks from successful executions (no extra model calls) to detect conflicts with skill state, repair affected content, validate updates, and rebuild when local repair is insufficient—without a description of the change being supplied. Directly about keeping a skill library useful as environments evolve.
mechanism: Selective maintenance of retained skill state after environment change: replay checks from successful executions detect conflicts, repair or rebuild outdated content, and validate updates, with no supplied description of the change.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across four task settings and two models, previously beneficial skills can reduce task performance by over 10 percentage points or increase execution cost by nearly 40% relative to no skill after environment changes. Relative to reusing stale state, selective maintenance is reported to improve task accuracy by up to 67pp and reduce execution steps by up to 37%.

title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
why: Automated scientific discovery with autonomous research units: a mutator agent creates idea lineages, and a local orchestrator periodically adapts the mutator's harness (or replaces its model / restarts idea evolution when progress stalls). Verifiers write verified improvements, useful components, and constraint violations into shared knowledge, the only channel between units—harness adaptation plus a retained, verified knowledge store.
mechanism: Decentralized self-improving research units: a local orchestrator periodically adapts a mutator agent's harness (or replaces the model / restarts evolution when stalled); verifiers admit improvements and constraints into a shared knowledge store that is the only inter-unit channel.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): evaluated on five research-cycle benchmarks—ScholarCatalyst, IdeaBench, IdeaScientist, EurekaBench, and SciLaws-Bench. Inventa is reported to lead all five, with 73.6% on EurekaBench versus 56.2% for CORAL, and 26.0 novel ideas per paper on IdeaBench versus 18.6 for ResearchAgent, with 82% fewer model calls.

title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
why: Couples evolution of complete executable safety harnesses with adaptive stressor evolution: utility-constrained, Pareto-scheduled tree search evolves harnesses from execution evidence while the task model, benchmark, tools, and evaluator stay fixed; adaptive stressors then discover utility-preserving attacks that guide a later harness-evolution stage. Co-evolution of a retained safety harness and an attack curriculum, first appearing in an owned category on this Wednesday list (primary cs.CR).
mechanism: Staged co-evolution of executable safety harnesses and adaptive injection stressors: tree search evolves harnesses from execution evidence under a utility constraint, then evolved stressors guide a subsequent harness-evolution stage, with the task model held fixed.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on AgentDyn with GPT-4o-mini, an evolved harness reduces attack success from 50.4% to 3.0% and improves clean and attacked utility over the initial harness. On Agent-SafetyBench with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, attack success falls from 82.6% to 62.0% while retaining helpfulness and runtime validity. Evolved harnesses transfer without further evolution to Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, reducing attack success from 32.1% to 0.9% while improving attacked-task utility.

title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
why: Asks whether capable frozen LLM agents still need an externally specified self-improvement loop. Given primitives, a compute budget, and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, the agent is allowed to construct its own context-based self-learning algorithm without an imposed loop or real-world data. The retained artifacts are learned text documents (and self-generated curricula), evaluated for transfer to external gameplay/navigation benchmarks. Also surfaced on HF Papers daily 18 Nov.
mechanism: Autonomous context-based self-improvement: a frozen LLM agent, given experience-collection and text-document-update tools plus a compute budget, constructs its own self-learning algorithm and retains learned text artifacts and self-generated curricula, without an externally imposed loop.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): in a gameplay testbed, sufficiently capable models are reported to self-improve under these conditions, with strategies aligned to self-regulated learning and self-generated curricula. Learned text artifacts are reported to transfer with improvement across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation (full numeric tables not in the listing/abs excerpt).

title: Simplicity Goes Far: Auditing Prompt Optimizers with Demonstration-Conditioned Prompt Search
why: Audit of automatic prompt optimizers (including policy-gradient, trace reflection, and evolutionary search / GEPA in DSPy-based compound systems). Isolates the shared generate-and-select step as Demonstration-Conditioned Prompt Search (DCPS), a mechanism-attribution control based on the APE recipe with no learned update, reflection, or evolution, and recommends reporting rollout, token, and dollar costs alongside accuracy.
mechanism: An audit control (DCPS) that freezes the prompt generator, conditions it on randomly sampled demonstrations, scores candidates on validation data, and keeps the best—used to attribute gains of heavier prompt-optimizer mechanisms versus generate-and-select sampling budget.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): DCPS replaces PPO in StablePrompt and is reported to match classification accuracy within 0.5 pp at roughly one-third the measured cost. In DSPy-based compound systems, under reported budgets, it matches GEPA's macro accuracy on GPT-4.1-mini while using 55% fewer rollouts at 32% lower measured API cost on average. Additional mechanisms are reported to retain advantages in some open-ended and reasoning-heavy settings.

title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
why: Negative-result / audit study of agent evolution loops that propose and select candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories). The Resolution Hypothesis holds that evolution often stalls because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify better artifacts, not because proposers fail to generate them. Calls for developing self-improving agents by making true improvements detectable and accumulable rather than only designing richer proposers.
mechanism: An evaluation-resolution audit of agent evolution: across methods that write candidate prompts, skills, or memories, selection under noisy scores is compared with random identification, and method rankings are compared with run-to-run margins.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), helpful candidate artifacts are reported to exist, but candidate-level selection is no better than random at separating helpful from harmful ones, so errors accumulate. At the method-ranking level, typical margins of a few percentage points are smaller than the difference between two independent runs of the same method.

title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
why: In-corpus replacement v1→v2 with method and experiment changes (not just wording). v2 specifies temporary fine-tuning probes, pooling accepted demonstrations across tasks to train a specialist VLA that works alongside the original executor, and summarizing each development round into shared experience for later diagnosis. New numbers and settings appear in the abstract (unseen composite success 13.8%→13.3%; new perturbed LIBERO-Pro 2.0 32.9%→49.1%; resource figures revised to 34% GPU time / 36% demonstrations) plus a new real-robot case (autonomous demo collection to recover fallen bottles).
mechanism: On-demand embodied RSI (update): a coding agent first refines tools and procedures, then uses temporary fine-tuning probes and pooled accepted demonstrations to train a specialist VLA alongside the original executor; round-level records are summarized into shared experience that guides later diagnosis and data collection.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abs): on unseen composite RoboCasa365 tasks, success rises from 4.6% to 13.3% (v1 abs reported 13.8%). On perturbed LIBERO-Pro 2.0 tasks (new in v2 abs), success rises from 32.9% to 49.1%. On Composite-Unseen, higher success than adapting every manipulation sub-step is reported using 34% of the GPU time and 36% of the demonstrations (v1 abs reported 28% GPU time and 22% demonstrations versus fine-tuning every sub-step). A real-robot experiment (new in v2 abs) reports autonomous demonstration collection and executor adaptation to recover fallen bottles.
